newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels may allow access to refugee camps.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels may allow access to refugee camps.

text.p: Zairean rebels said they might allow aid workers on Thursday to reach two camps south of Kisangani where villagers reported fierce fighting between refugees and rebel forces.

The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR and some journalists were told by rebel authorities to be on standby for a visit to the camps, sealed off since Monday. UNHCR fears many of the 80,000 refugees south of Kisangani have already fled because of the fighting.

The rebels' apparent decision to allow access to the camps came after U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said he was "shocked and appalled by the inhumanity" of their action which he said was killing the refugees by starvation.
Zairean villagers said on Wednesday Tutsi-dominated rebels had killed many Rwandan Hutu refugees at Kasese, 25 km (15 miles) south of Kisangani, where 55,000 were in makeshift camps.
They said a pitched battle between rebels and refugees accompanied the slaughter on Tuesday at camps near Kasese.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila dismissed the reports as "total nonsense", saying Rwandan Hutu militiamen among the refugees attacked villagers and rebels intervened to stop the fighting.
Aid workers have accused the rebels of orchestrating attacks on aid vehicles and looting of aid since Friday after delaying until May 5 a U.N. airlift of up to 100,000 refugees south of Kisangani.
Annan told reporters in New York on Wednesday that the refugees lived in deplorable conditions and promises to allow humanitarian agencies to help them had not been kept.
"I have therefore appealed to the international community to work with me in pressing Kabila and those in the region who back him, to push him to allow assistance to the refugees.

"I do not think the international community can stand by as thousands of men and women and children are starved to death. You can kill by shooting or by starvation. Killing by starvation is what is going on," Annan said.
"If Mr Kabila is in charge of his forces, he has to bring them under control. If he is not, he should take measures to control them."
Earlier, UNHCR and other agencies expressed deep concern over the reports from Zairean villagers that the rebels might have killed many of Rwandan Hutu refugees near Kisangani.
"We are hearing unconfirmed reports of large-scale killings around camps we have had no access to since last Sunday, and we are deeply concerned," UNHCR spokeswoman Pam O'Toole said.
Alphonse Soku, a farmer, told Reuters the rebels went into one of the camps on Tuesday morning.
"They killed many, many refugees -- hundreds. There was lots of shooting all morning," he said. "They used a mechanical digger to bury the bodies."
The Hutus fled Rwanda in 1994 and are collectively accused by minority Tutsis of genocide in Rwanda in the same year.
They arrived at their Kasese camps in mid-March after six months of trekking over volcanic rock and through bush and jungle in a vain attempt to flee the Tutsi-backed rebels.
The refugees have fled 600 km (375 miles) since last October and more than 1,500 have died at the camps south of Kisangani. 240808 GMT apr 97
